# @sinyotsai/opencode-tokenusage

Shows the current session's token usage, generation speed, time to first token, and the model that actually answered — in the opencode TUI sidebar.

opencode reports the model you *asked for*. When the provider routes through LiteLLM, the real model only appears in the HTTP response header `x-litellm-model-name`. This plugin reads that header and puts the answer on screen.

## Cards

| Card | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Real model** | The model behind the latest main-agent request in this session, plus the routing tier and that request's cost when LiteLLM routed it |
| **Token Usage** | Token totals for this session and all its subagents, cache rate, TTFT, Last TPS, Avg TPS, and a per-model breakdown |

## Requirements

- opencode **2.2.0 or newer** (verified on 2.2.7)
- V2 only. V1 used a different plugin hook mechanism and is not supported.
- Accurate TPS needs opencode **2.3.0 or newer**, which records `time.firstToken` on each assistant message. On older versions the rates still render, but they read low (see [Metric definitions](#metric-definitions)).

## Installation

opencode runs its server and TUI as separate processes, so the same plugin must be registered in both places.

1. **Server** — edit `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` and add to the `plugins` array:

   ```jsonc
   "plugins": [
     "@sinyotsai/opencode-tokenusage@latest"
   ]
   ```

2. **TUI** — edit `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` and add the same package:

   ```json
   {
     "plugins": [
       "@sinyotsai/opencode-tokenusage@latest"
     ]
   }
   ```

On Windows the config directory is `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode`.

Restart opencode and the `Real model` and `Token Usage` cards appear in the sidebar. `opencode plugin list` confirms the plugin loaded.

> Use the same package name in both files — no `/server` or `/tui` suffix; opencode picks the right entry point for its runtime. Registering both a local directory and the npm package loads the plugin twice. Pinning an exact version (e.g. `@0.2.0`) fails to resolve on some opencode installers; use `@latest`.

## Usage

### Real model

Shows the model used by the latest **main-agent** request in this session.

- When the response carries LiteLLM's `x-litellm-model-name`, the card shows the model after routing, with the routing tier and that request's cost.
- Without that header it shows the model opencode requested, rendered **dimmed** to mark it as unverified.
- A new session shows `-` until the first response arrives.
- Subagent, title-generation and compaction requests never overwrite this card.

### Token Usage

Aggregates usage across this session and every subagent, grouped by `providerID/modelID`.

Collapsed view:

- `Cache` — cache hit rate with a progress bar
- `Input` / `Output` — token totals
- `TTFT` — time to first token
- `Last TPS` — generation speed of the most recent completed request
- `Avg TPS` — average generation speed for the whole session

Click `> show detail` for the per-model breakdown (`Cache`, `Reqs`, `Input`, `Output`, `Avg TPS`); click `v hide detail` to collapse it.

#### Metric definitions

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| `Cache` | `cache.read / (input + cache.read)`; shows `-` when the denominator is 0 |
| `Input` | Uncached input + `cache.read` |
| `Output` | Output tokens, excluding reasoning |
| `TTFT` | Mean time to first token, weighted by request count |
| `Last TPS` | Generation speed of the most recent completed request; `-` when it cannot be computed |
| `Avg TPS` | Σ generated tokens ÷ Σ generation time across all requests, subagents included |

Generation speed is the number of tokens the model actually produced (**output + reasoning**) divided by the time it actually spent producing them.

That time runs from the first token to request completion, minus the time tools spent running. Overlapping parallel tool calls are merged, so the same wall-clock second is never subtracted twice. Messages from before opencode 2.3.0 carry no first-token timestamp and fall back to "request created → completed", which includes queueing and tool time — their rates read low.

Cache rate colours: green at 50% or above, yellow from 20% to 50%, red below 20%, following the active theme. The breakdown lists every model; variants of one model are merged into a single row.

## Privacy and data

- The plugin reads response headers only. It never reads or rewrites response bodies, and never stores API keys, prompts or conversation content.
- Model records are kept per session:
  - Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode-tokenusage`
  - Other platforms: `${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/opencode-tokenusage`
- Files are named `model-<sessionID>.json` and contain the model name, routing info and a timestamp.
- You can delete that directory with opencode closed; past session files are not pruned automatically.
- On POSIX the directory is created `0700` and files `0600`; on Windows the user profile ACL applies.

## Known limitations

- `Real model` only reflects the latest main-agent request in the current session. It keeps no history and does not aggregate across sessions.
- `Token Usage` covers only the current session and its subagents, not other sessions.
- Model names are resolved from the LiteLLM response header alone. Providers that do not route through LiteLLM, or omit that header, show the requested name (dimmed). To avoid breaking the stream, the plugin never reads the `model` field from the response body.
- `google-vertex` has not been verified on V2.
- `cache.write` is not displayed: every provider tested reports 0.
- Several opencode instances open on the same session share that session's model record.
